key_insight: DANO learns configuration-dependent nonlocal interactions from field data, enabling full-field prediction and inverse design in heterogeneous metamaterials.
engineering_relevance: Demonstrated on optical metasurfaces, the approach could inform scalable design of nonlocal multiscale systems, though fracture and damage applications remain untested here.
method: Uses a domain-decomposition attention neural operator.
Learns interactions in heterogeneous systems governed by linear field equations.
Interrogates learned interactions using physics-based validation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports full-field prediction across geometric heterogeneity and drive conditions, small-to-large domain transfer, and multifunctional inverse design in large-scale optical metasurfaces.
watch_item: Applicability to nonlinear fracture and damage is not established by the reported linear-field optical case study.
paper_title: Learning Nonlocal Interactions in Large-Scale Heterogeneous Metamaterials through Scientific Machine Learning
